gloss: way one uses one's hands; hand movements

definitions.gloss: way one uses one's hands; hand movements
definitions.explanation: The visible manner in which someone moves their hands while doing something. Almost always used with a modifier that judges the movement as skilled, clumsy, gentle, and so on.

examples.japanese: {慣|な}れた{手|て}つきで{魚|さかな}をさばく。
examples.english: To fillet a fish with practiced hands.

examples.japanese: {危|あぶ}なっかしい{手|て}つきで{包丁|ほうちょう}を{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: He is using the kitchen knife with an alarmingly clumsy grip.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{優|やさ}しい{手|て}つきで{赤|あか}ちゃんを{抱|だ}き{上|あ}げ、そっと{布団|ふとん}に{寝|ね}かせた。
examples.english: She picked the baby up with gentle hands and laid it softly on the futon.

notes:
Nearly always appears as 「{modifier}な{手|て}つきで」 describing how an action is performed. It is about the look of the movement, not about the hands themselves.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {慣|な}れた{手|て}つき: practiced, assured hand movements
- {危|あぶ}なっかしい{手|て}つき: clumsy, unsafe-looking handling
- {優|やさ}しい{手|て}つき: gentle hands
- {鮮|あざ}やかな{手|て}つき: deft, impressive handling

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手|て}さばき: handling, dexterity — emphasizes technique and speed, typically praising skill
- {仕草|しぐさ}: gesture, mannerism — any bodily movement or habit, not limited to the hands
